customer_acme: hey @support — we're seeing small but consistent daily mismatches between the dashboard daily totals and the CSV export for our org (AcmeCorp). totals in the web UI for 2026-03-14 show 1,210,345 tokens, CSV export for the same day shows 1,207,890 tokens. this started ~2026-03-10. we use timezone Asia/Kathmandu (UTC+05:45). any ideas?
alyssa: thanks — can you attach a sample export and the org id? which report is it (daily usage / per-project)?
customer_acme: attaching a snippet (pasted below). org id: org_0acme. it's the daily usage CSV (per-org). look at timestamps around midnight: rows for 2026-03-13 include several events with timestamps like 2026-03-13T23:58:12Z and 2026-03-14T00:03:21Z — seems ~45min boundary causing some tokens to land on previous day in UI.
customer_acme: CSV snippet:
"timestamp,project_id,tokens
2026-03-13T23:58:12Z,proj_acme_a,1245
2026-03-14T00:03:21Z,proj_acme_a,980
"
alyssa: got it — that definitely smells like a timezone/day-boundary bug. tagging eng: @chao @benji. metrics-bot: can you run the usage-aggregation query for org_0acme for Mar 13-14 and paste the raw row counts? :eyes:
metrics-bot: query job queued (job_id=uq-1899991). will post result shortly.
metrics-bot: result: 
"2026-03-13, total_tokens, 1,207,890
2026-03-14, total_tokens, 1,210,345"
chao: quick hypothesis — our daily bucketing logic converts UTC timestamps to org tz, then floors to midnight by truncating hours (i.e. subtracting hours offset only). that would work for whole-hour zones but break for minute-offset zones like +05:45.
benji: example of current bug (pseudo-java):
```java
ZoneOffset offset = ZoneId.of(orgTz).getRules().getOffset(instant);
int hourOffset = offset.getTotalSeconds() / 3600; // drops minutes
ZonedDateTime local = instant.atZone(ZoneOffset.UTC).minusHours(hourOffset);
LocalDate day = local.toLocalDate();
```
chao: yep — the getTotalSeconds/3600 truncation is the culprit. should be using instant.atZone(ZoneId.of(orgTz)).toLocalDate() or apply the full offset including minutes.
alyssa: nice find. do we have a quick patch we can try in staging and a repro? customer provided good repro data.
chao: I'll open INF-2042 and push a small fix to the aggregation service: replace manual offset math with zone-aware conversion. will add unit tests for zones with minute offsets (+05:45, +12:45 etc.) and a regression CSV diff test.
benji: once patch is up I'll run the nightly aggregation for org_0acme on staging and compare totals.
metrics-bot: staging run queued (job_id=uq-stg-1899991).
metrics-bot: staging result (post-patch): 
"2026-03-13, total_tokens, 1,210,343
2026-03-14, total_tokens, 1,207,892"
alyssa: staging totals look swapped relative to original; numbers now align with raw events assigned by local date. @customer_acme — can you confirm these corrected totals mirror what you expect when you convert event timestamps to Asia/Kathmandu local date?
customer_acme: quick check: yes, when we convert the raw timestamps to Asia/Kathmandu and group by date we get: 2026-03-13 -> 1,210,343 and 2026-03-14 -> 1,207,892. that matches staging. thanks! :pray:
alyssa: plan: 1) merge patch to prod aggregation service with a feature flag off, 2) run a backfill job to re-aggregate the last 30 days for orgs with non-hour offsets, 3) enable flag. will post ETA.
chao: assigning to myself for the patch and to infra for backfill. cc @benji for validation.
alyssa: ETA on backfill / rollout is EOD tomorrow unless infra hits rate limits. I'll keep you posted.
customer_acme: appreciate the fast turnaround. please ping when fixed and if we need to re-download reports.
alyssa: will do. tracking INF-2042 and will DM when prod backfill completes. :white_check_mark:
